source.paper: Calizo, Balandin, Bao, Miao, Lau 2007, Nano Lett. 7, 2645, arXiv:0708.1223; Cancado, Jorio, Martins Ferreira, Stavale, Achete, Capaz, Moutinho, Lombardo, Kulmala, Ferrari 2011, Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies, Nano Lett. 11, 3190, doi:10.1021/nl201432g, arXiv:1105.0175; Lee, Ahn, Shim, Lee, Ryu 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024, arXiv:1209.0234
source.locator: Calizo abstract and Table I (temperature coefficients); Cancado p.2 (power kept about 1 mW to avoid heating); Lee 2012 (strain and doping from G and 2D)

items.text: G and 2D both move down and broaden monotonically with laser power on the same spot, while the Si line stays put: the trend tracks power, which points to laser heating of the flake rather than a property of the graphene
items.locator: Calizo 2007 p.3 (G and 2D shift down with increasing temperature) and p.4-5 (temperature change from increased excitation power); Cancado p.2

items.text: Estimates the temperature rise from the G shift with chi_G about -0.016 cm-1/K: about 50 K at 2 mW and 125 K at 5 mW above the 0.5 mW spectrum (the 2D with about -0.034 cm-1/K gives a consistent estimate)
items.locator: Calizo 2007 abstract and Table I (single layer, 83 to 373 K)

items.text: In a G vs 2D position plot the power series moves along a line of slope about 2 to 3 (Calizo's coefficients give 0.034/0.016, about 2.1), close to the strain line (about 2.2) of the Lee 2012 vector analysis, so that analysis applied naively would misread the heating as strain
Positions measured at different powers cannot be compared or fed into a strain/doping (G vs 2D) analysis without correcting for heating; use the lowest power, or a power series extrapolated to zero
Recommends checking that the lowest-power spectrum is in the linear (heating-free) regime, e.g. by measuring at one more lower power, and asks about the spot size or power density
items.locator: Cancado p.2 (about 1 mW with a 100x objective to avoid heating)

items.text: Uses the 0.5 mW spectrum (G about 1582, 2D about 2668 cm-1 at 532 nm) as the reference and finds it close to unstrained, undoped graphene within the uncertainty of the laser-wavelength correction of 2D
items.locator: Lee 2012 origin (1581.6, 2676.9) at 514.5 nm; Cancado p.5 (2D dispersion about 104 cm-1/eV)

wrong_claims.text: Attributes the power-dependent shifts to strain or doping of the sample
Recommends the highest-power spectrum for analysis because it has the best signal

notes: Synthetic, 532 nm. Low-power spectrum: G 1581.6 (Lee 2012 origin; G is not dispersive in stage 1, Cancado Fig. 5b) and 2D 2668.6 cm-1 (Lee 2012 origin 2676.9 at 514.5 nm moved to 532 nm with 2 x 52 cm-1/eV, Cancado p.5). FWHM G 14.0 (Cancado p.5-6), 2D 32.0 (Fig. 5a reading). Temperature rises {0.5: 0.0, 2.0: 50.0, 5.0: 125.0} K (curator); shifts and broadening per power {0.5: (-0.0, -0.0, 0.0), 2.0: (-0.8, -1.7000000000000002, 1.5), 5.0: (-2.0, -4.25, 3.75)} (dG, d2D, extra G FWHM in cm-1) are curator values from Calizo's coefficients and curator temperature rises; the extra width is curator. Calizo measured at 488 nm on graphene on SiO2/Si; applying the coefficients at 532 nm is an assumption. The Si line is not shifted. Items f2 and n1 depend on Lee 2012, whose numbers come from the verified-numbers file, not a re-reading.
